output.subject: Your complaint about your father's account
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for writing to us about your father. We're sorry for the distress this has caused you and your family.

We have received your complaint. You told us that on September 2 your father, who is 82, received a call from someone pretending to be his grandson, who said he had been arrested and needed bail. You mentioned that over the next two days your father withdrew $4,000 and then $5,000 in cash at the Depot Square branch and handed the money to a "courier" who came to his home. You said that no one at the branch asked him any questions, even though he has never taken out more than a few hundred dollars at a time in forty years.

You also told us that you hold power of attorney for your father. You have asked what Meridian Harbor Bank will do about this and what safeguards we have in place for elderly customers.

A specialist team is reviewing your complaint and will respond to you within 10 business days.

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: The writer is the account holder's child, not the account holder. Confirm whether ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧ will resolve to the writer or to the father before sending.
Verify the power of attorney is on file and valid before sharing any account details with the writer.
Confirm the dates, the branch, and the two withdrawals ($4,000 and $5,000, $9,000 total) against account records.
Decide whether the response should advise reporting the scam to police, if it has not already been reported.
Consider whether the father's accounts need immediate protective steps, as he may be targeted again.
The customer has asked what the bank will do about the loss and about safeguards for elderly customers. The specialist team must decide how to answer both.
